cost.note: public read endpoints only; no API key, payment, or transaction

observation.does_not_show: It does not show another venue, future yield, position-specific earnings, a submitted move, or a paired run against a person.
observation.method: The catalogue yield-router runner read the PancakeSwap explorer top list and token allowlist at 2026-08-22T16:05:30+00:00, applied the stated TVL, turnover, token, and fee-data gates, and compared 26 eligible pools of 35 considered. The comparison-only path made no BSC eth_call, so it reports no chain block.
observation.population: 26 eligible pools of 35 considered from https://explorer.pancakeswap.com/api/cached/pools/v3/bsc/list/top at 2026-08-22T16:05:30+00:00
observation.time_source: PancakeSwap explorer snapshot time reported by the service
observation.window: single recorded read; no paired run against a person; one explorer top-pools snapshot

payment.note: No payment, signature, transaction, or network write was made.

break_even.cost_covers: the caller's own figure, in USD. It has to cover gas on every leg, the swap's own pool fee and its price impact at this size, and any fees left uncollected in the pool being left. Docket reads no BNB price here and does not invent one, so this number is supplied rather than derived — and a break-even is only as good as it is
break_even.method: days_to_recover = switching_cost_usd / (position_size_usd x (candidate_net_apr - current_net_apr) / 365). Both rates are the 24h observed net figures annualised by x365. within_horizon compares that against a horizon of 30 days, which is a stated choice rather than a derived one — the inputs are all here, so a reader can apply a different horizon without asking.

candidates.net_vs_gross: net is the fee less the protocol's own reported cut. Liquidity providers keep roughly two thirds of what a pool charges, so the gross figure beside this overstates what is kept by about half again
candidates.rate_denominator: the pool's own reported TVL in USD. It is a property of the pool and not of any position in it — a concentrated position earns at this rate only while it is in range and earns nothing while it is not
candidates.rate_window: 24h of fees annualised by x365, one observation and not a forecast: a quiet day reads as a permanently poor pool and a busy one as a fortune

candidates.rate_window: 24h of fees annualised by x365, one observation and not a forecast: a quiet day reads as a permanently poor pool and a busy one as a fortune

break_even.cost_covers: the caller's own figure, in USD. It has to cover gas on every leg, the swap's own pool fee and its price impact at this size, and any fees left uncollected in the pool being left. Docket reads no BNB price here and does not invent one, so this number is supplied rather than derived — and a break-even is only as good as it is
break_even.method: days_to_recover = switching_cost_usd / (position_size_usd x (candidate_net_apr - current_net_apr) / 365). Both rates are the 24h observed net figures annualised by x365. within_horizon compares that against a horizon of 30 days, which is a stated choice rather than a derived one — the inputs are all here, so a reader can apply a different horizon without asking.
break_even.reason: this pool's observed net rate is not above the current one, so there is nothing extra to recover the 15.0 cost from
